summary: Android port: MilestoneDto.nextOccurrence compares the milestone's local midnight with the current instant, so from 00:01 on the milestone day the next occurrence is a year away; the Milestones row computes days from the instant (day before reads 0d, day itself reads 364d) and NotificationPlanner drops the 9 AM 'today' ping when a reschedule runs that morning. Same defect as the iOS bug fixed on this branch (android/app/src/main/java/com/jackwallner/bond/model/Completion.kt:63, ui/screens/Milestones.kt:139).

guard: CatchUpTests.aReminderFetchThatFails_keepsTheAlarmsThatAreArmed and aLaunchWithNoSignalAtAll_keepsTheAlarmsThatAreArmed (with aListThatLoads_replacesTheAlarms_evenWhenItIsEmpty so the guard cannot over-block)
summary: Android port: MainActivity.onResume runs reminders.refresh() then graph.rescheduleNotifications() whether or not the refresh succeeded; AlarmNotificationScheduler.reschedule removes every non-milestone alarm before re-arming from the list, so a cold start with no signal (empty list) cancels all scheduled reminders. Same defect as the iOS bug fixed on this branch (MainActivity.kt:88-92, data/Notifications.kt:56).

Android port: milestones are only fetched (and their 7-day, 1-day and day-of alarms only armed) from the Milestones screen (ui/screens/Milestones.kt:83), so a device whose user has not opened that screen since install, such as the partner's phone, never gets the pings the empty state promises. iOS had the same gap and is fixed on this branch by loading milestones when home appears.

iOS and Android: 'Reschedule' / 'Pick a time' on a partner's request cannot be saved. The editor upserts the partner-authored row (ReminderEditorView.save, repo.upsert; Android Reminders.kt PartnerRequestCard onEdit, ReminderEditor.kt:203), but supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql only lets the author write: reminders_member_insert needs author_id = auth.uid() and reminders_author_update / reminders_author_delete are author-only, and no later migration changes them. The target's save therefore fails with a row-level security error shown in the form, and a swipe-delete on a partner request removes the row locally while the server keeps it (it returns on the next refresh). Proven against the checked-in schema; not run against a database (no Postgres on the fleet host, production may differ).

iOS: a reminder written for the partner only reaches their phone if their app runs between its creation and its time. Reminders become local notifications armed on the target's phone from the list that app fetched (NotificationScheduler.reschedule arms targetId == self only), and the list is only fetched while the app is open (launch, return to the foreground, pull to refresh, the realtime feed). Nothing registers for remote notifications (no registerForRemoteNotifications call, no aps-environment entitlement, profiles.apns_token is never written), so SupabaseFunctions/send-push has no token to send to, and there is no background refresh. 'Surprise (hidden from partner)' reminders can never be armed at all: reminders_member_select hides the row from the target. The editor, the templates (which target the partner for paired users), the watch and the marketing copy ('Set nudges for your partner') present partner delivery as working. docs/MVP_TRIAGE.md B3 already records it and offers shipping local-only with a caveat; the app has no caveat. Android documents the same limit (.claude/rules/android.md, 'Not ported').
